package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of these packages contain vulnerabilities that allow attackers to craft malicious npm packages which, when installed or extracted, can overwrite arbitrary files on the filesystem. This can lead to arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the user running npm install, even if lifecycle scripts are disabled.

execution_context.file_location: npm package archive (.tar.gz/.tgz) with malicious file paths

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package extraction, the code processes archive entries with directory traversal sequences (e.g., ../../), causing files to be written outside the intended directory, potentially overwriting sensitive system files.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of directory traversal in archive entries is a classic technique to escape the intended extraction directory and overwrite arbitrary files.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package extraction should only write files within the target directory. Malicious behavior occurs when extraction code fails to sanitize paths, allowing writes outside this directory.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate archives should never contain directory traversal sequences in file paths.
key_indicators: Archive entries with '../' or absolute paths
Extraction code that does not sanitize or validate file paths

execution_context.file_location: npm package archive (.tar.gz/.tgz) with symlink entries

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During package extraction, the code processes symlink entries that point to sensitive files (e.g., /etc/passwd), enabling subsequent archive entries to overwrite these files via the symlink.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Symlinks in archives that point to sensitive or system files are a known attack vector for file overwrite and privilege escalation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal extraction should not allow symlinks to escape the intended directory or point to system files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Symlinks may be used in legitimate packages, but should never point outside the package directory.
key_indicators: Symlink entries in archives pointing to absolute or parent directories
Lack of symlink resolution checks in extraction code

attack_chain.action: Attacker crafts a malicious npm package archive with directory traversal or symlink entries.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious archive is published to npm or distributed directly.

attack_chain.action: User installs the malicious package using npm CLI, triggering extraction of the archive.
attack_chain.leads_to: Extraction code in tar/arborist processes malicious paths.

attack_chain.action: Extraction code fails to sanitize paths, allowing files to be written outside the intended directory or to sensitive locations.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary files are overwritten, potentially leading to code execution or system compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Archive extraction with file paths containing '../' or absolute paths
Symlink creation during archive extraction pointing outside the target directory
Unexpected file overwrites during npm install
file_indicators: npm package archives (.tar.gz/.tgz) with directory traversal in file paths
Symlink entries in npm package archives pointing to system files
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm package extraction for archive entries containing directory traversal sequences (../) or symlinks pointing outside the intended extraction directory. Flag or block packages that attempt to write files outside the node_modules directory or create symlinks to sensitive system locations. Use updated versions of tar and arborist that patch these vulnerabilities.
